title: Foreign Versus Local Companies that Qualify Under Condition 1 of Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities Scheme
what_it_is: Foreign Versus Local Companies that Qualify Under Condition 1 of Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities Scheme

sections.label: M-SEP beneficiary business entities
sections.summary: M-SEP beneficiaries are locally incorporated or registered business entities, required to hire Work Permit or S Pass holders to benefit from the scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: All Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities (M-SEP) beneficiaries are locally incorporated or registered business entities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: They would need to be as such in order to hire Work Permit or S Pass holders to benefit from the M-SEP scheme.

sections.label: M-SEP eligibility and local shareholding
sections.summary: Condition 1 lists 16 programmes; about 40% of eligible firms have at least 30% local shareholding, which is not a prerequisite for M-SEP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Under Condition 1, in terms of fulfilment of the M-SEP scheme, there are 16 programmes that are listed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Of the firms today that are currently eligible for M-SEP, about 40% of them have local shareholding of at least 30%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Having local shareholding is not a prerequisite for M-SEP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: What is more important in the entire M-SEP scheme is that they contribute to our growth and they create opportunities for Singaporeans.

sections.label: M-SEP work pass concentration
sections.summary: The passage states over-concentration will not happen, as EDB and ESG work closely with companies and M-SEP work passes will not move the needle significantly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If you are going to look at one particular aspect of the entire plethora of schemes that we have available and say that this particular scheme is going to result in over-concentration, that is not going to happen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: These are companies that EDB and ESG work very closely with and the number of work passes that is going to be awarded through M-SEP would not move the needle significantly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: It is really meant to see how we can provide these companies to have a leg-up to fulfil our strategic economic priorities.
